reference.title: Push-up to Side Plank
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Chest, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press; breathe out as you turn into the side plank.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, 1 s up, 1 s to rotate, 1 s hold, 0.9 s back

prescription.tempo: Controlled; 1 s hold in each side plank
prescription.progression: Longer side-plank holds, then a light dumbbell in each hand (renegade-style), then feet stacked

cues.text: High plank, hands under the shoulders, feet hip width apart on the balls of the feet.
Breathe in and do a strict push-up: elbows about 45 degrees, body in one line.
Breathe out and press to straight arms.
Shift onto one hand and turn the whole body as one piece, pivoting onto the sides of the feet.
Side plank: support hand under the shoulder, hips high, free arm reaching to the ceiling; eyes follow the top hand.
Lower the arm and turn back into the plank with control, then repeat to the other side.

mistakes.mistake: Hips dropping in the side plank
mistakes.fix: Push the floor away and lift the hips so the body is straight from head to feet.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the shoulders first and leaving the hips behind
mistakes.fix: Rotate shoulders and hips together, like a log.

mistakes.mistake: Support hand ahead of the shoulder
mistakes.fix: Keep the support wrist under the shoulder.
Pause one second in each side plank.
Brace through the push-up as in a strict push-up.

kinematics.norm: Arms straight but not locked at the top; elbows to about 90 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees: from facing the floor to facing sideways, shoulders and hips turning together (clinical opinion)
Wrist under the shoulder, arm vertical, elbow straight in the side plank (clinical opinion)
Reaches straight up toward the ceiling, in line with the support arm (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Hip height in the side plank
kinematics.norm: Hips lifted in line with the shoulders and feet; the side bridge is a high oblique and gluteus medius exercise (Ekstrom 2007; Youdas 2008)
Controlled with a short hold in each side plank (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #066412, Push-up to Side Plank, video (movement reference)

cautions: Wrist pain: the planted palm bends the wrist back about 80-90 degrees; use push-up handles or hex dumbbells to keep the wrists straight, or stop if pain persists (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain: keep the elbows tucked rather than flared out to the sides, and shorten the range if needed (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Support shoulder: keep it pushed away from the floor in the side plank, not sinking toward the ear (clinical opinion).
modify: Shorten the rotation (a half turn) or drop the bottom knee in the side plank.
Wrist pain: hex dumbbells as handles.
regressions: Push-up then side plank on the forearm.
progressions: Feet stacked in the side plank.
Light dumbbells in the hands (T push-up with dumbbells).

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher: lowers the body under control and drives it back up.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pusher: lowers the body under control and drives it back up.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows on the way up and brakes them on the way down.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows on the way up and brakes them on the way down.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest muscles.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest muscles.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the support shoulder blade on the rib cage through the rotation.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the support shoulder blade on the rib cage through the rotation.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the hips from sagging or piking: the body moves as one plank.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Hold the side plank and control the rotation; the side bridge gave high external and internal oblique activity in EMG studies (Ekstrom 2007; Youdas 2008).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Hold the side plank and control the rotation; the side bridge gave high external and internal oblique activity in EMG studies (Ekstrom 2007; Youdas 2008).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Control the shoulder blades as they draw together on the way down.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Control the shoulder blades as they draw together on the way down.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Steadies the support shoulder as the body turns over the hand.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Steadies the support shoulder as the body turns over the hand.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Squeezed lightly to keep the pelvis in line (no sag).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Squeezed lightly to keep the pelvis in line (no sag).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight so the legs stay part of the plank.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight so the legs stay part of the plank.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold a long, neutral spine and neck.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold a long, neutral spine and neck.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the hips lifted in the side plank (the side bridge gave high gluteus medius activity, Ekstrom 2007).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the hips lifted in the side plank (the side bridge gave high gluteus medius activity, Ekstrom 2007).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Holds the support arm and lifts the free arm toward the ceiling.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Holds the support arm and lifts the free arm toward the ceiling.
